name: present progressive
title: Spanish Present Progressive Practice: Estar + -ando, -iendo Quiz
description: Practice the Spanish present progressive: estar + -ando or -iendo, gerunds like leyendo and durmiendo, pronouns and when not to use it, with 10 quiz sentences.
answer: The Spanish present progressive is estar in the present plus a gerund: estoy hablando, estás comiendo, están escribiendo. -ar verbs take -ando and -er and -ir verbs take -iendo. Use it for actions in progress right now. Unlike English, Spanish does not use it for future plans: «I'm leaving tomorrow» is «salgo mañana».

rulesCaption: Forming and using the present progressive

rules.example: leer → leyendo, oír → oyendo, traer → trayendo
dormir → durmiendo, pedir → pidiendo, decir → diciendo

rules.meaning: before estar or attached, with accent

quiz.why: Leer: the i becomes y, leyendo.
Dormir changes o to u in the gerund: durmiendo.
Direct object la attached, with an accent on the gerund.
Future plans take the present or ir a, not the progressive.

mistakes: Using ser instead of estar: «soy comiendo» should be «estoy comiendo».
Forgetting the y in some gerunds: «leiendo» and «creiendo» should be «leyendo» and «creyendo».
Using the progressive for the future: «estoy saliendo mañana» should be «salgo mañana» or «voy a salir mañana».
Missing the accent when a pronoun is attached: «estoy haciendolo» should be «estoy haciéndolo».
Overusing it for states: «estoy teniendo un carro» should be «tengo un carro».

heritage: Heritage speakers in the US sometimes use the progressive for the future or for states, under English influence: «estoy teniendo problemas» is common and understood, but «tengo problemas» is more natural in Spanish. Also check the accent when you attach pronouns: diciéndome.
teacher: Show a busy picture (a park, a kitchen, a street) and have students say what each person is doing with está + gerund. Then a partner guesses who they are describing.

faq.question: How do you form the gerund in Spanish?
faq.answer: Drop -ar and add -ando (hablando), drop -er or -ir and add -iendo (comiendo, viviendo). When the stem ends in a vowel, -iendo becomes -yendo (leyendo), and -ir verbs with a stem change show it (durmiendo, pidiendo).

faq.question: When should I use the progressive and when the simple present?
faq.answer: Use the progressive to stress that something is happening right now. The simple present also covers the present moment (¿Qué haces?), and it is the only option for habits and future plans.

faq.question: Can I use other verbs instead of estar?
faq.answer: Yes, at higher levels: seguir + gerund (sigo estudiando, I'm still studying), llevar + time + gerund (llevo un año trabajando aquí) and ir + gerund (va mejorando, it's gradually improving).
